authoring_notes.structure: 59 chapters across 7 tracks. Foundations + systems front-loaded. Synthetic led by the design-pattern chapter before modality surveys. SFT principles before case studies. RL consolidated into method families, not per-paper variants. Evaluation promoted to a first-class track. Content tracks (foundations, data, synthetic, sft, rl, eval) each end with a lab chapter; the Infra track ends with a capstone (ch-59) instead of a lab.
authoring_notes.track_ordering: Tracks are loosely sequential. Within a track, deps are strictly sequential. Foundations must come first. Eval can in principle be pulled forward once the learner has reached SFT.
authoring_notes.chapter_types: Each chapter has an explicit 'kind' field: 'content' for read-and-discuss chapters (5-6 concepts), 'lab' for hands-on track-end chapters that require producing an artifact (filter pipeline, synthetic set, SFT run, RL experiment, eval harness, framework read-through), and 'capstone' (exactly one, ch-57) for the final end-to-end reproduction.
authoring_notes.per_chapter_format: Each read.md quotes real code/equations from the raw-data library and extracts the chapter's core insight + guideline. Chapters may emit companion HTML files under ch-XX/figures/ or ch-XX/animations/ for architecture diagrams, parameter explorers, or step-by-step animations (see CLAUDE.md 'Chapter authoring — HTML visualizations').
authoring_notes.depth_target: Read pages should be long and source-rich — multiple source quotes, full equations, concrete hyperparameters extracted from model reports.
authoring_notes.intended_format: Flagship self-study program for someone targeting research-engineering or training-engineering work at a strong AI lab. Not a bootcamp, not a casual survey. Expect multi-month progression at the learner's own pace. It can also be consumed as three shorter specializations (Foundations+Data+Synthetic; SFT+RL; Eval+Infra+Capstone) if the learner needs to slice it that way.
authoring_notes.rl_vs_eval_boundary: RL track covers reward and judge topics as they are used during optimization — RM training, reward hacking, judge-driven preference loops, Constitutional AI, RLAIF. Eval track covers judges as measurement instruments — calibration, position/verbosity/self-enhancement bias audits, contamination workflow, slice analysis, go/no-go memos. If a topic is about producing a signal for training, it belongs in RL; if it is about auditing or comparing checkpoints, it belongs in Eval.
authoring_notes.data_vs_infra_replay_boundary: Data track handles replay as dataset / prompt-source design — which prompts to keep, how to mine difficulty, how to mix old vs new prompts. Infra track handles replay as runtime / systems architecture — replay buffers in the trainer, on-policy vs off-policy sampling, async rollout queues. They share the word but not the concern.
authoring_notes.lab_paths: Every lab chapter offers two paths. Full-budget path: multi-GPU, 1B–3B model, end-to-end run. Resource-constrained path: single-node or single-GPU, 125M–1B model, partial reproduction with replayed logs or precomputed rollouts where feasible. The memo/artifact requirement is the same in both paths — only the training scale differs.
